entities.summary: Henrietta Cuttino Dozier (1872–1947) was an American architect in Atlanta, Georgia, and Jacksonville, Florida. She is considered the first female architect in the state of Georgia and was the first woman in the Southern United States to receive formal architectural training from a national school of architecture. She designed churches, schools, government buildings, apartments and houses.
